proof:
Write $D(s)=\operatorname{dist}(s,I)$, $q_j=j^{-1}-e^{-2j}$ and $v=t-q_j$. Convexity of $D$ gives convex bodies and the raw affine parameter $v$ is at least $e^{-2j}$. The volume element in $(s,t,x/t)$ is $t\,ds\,dt\,d(x/t)$. The primitive $v^2\log v/2-v^2/4+q_j(v\log v-v)$ for $t\log v$ tends uniformly to $-1/4$ at the upper endpoint and to zero at the lower endpoint. This gives the claimed normalization. The lower roof graph has surface area density $(j^{-1}+e^{-j}D)\sqrt{2+e^{-2j}|D'|^2}$ in $s,x/t$, and its outward normal converges uniformly wherever defined to $n_0$. There $v=e^{-j}D(s)+e^{-2j}$, so $(-\log L_j)_+/j$ is uniformly bounded and tends to $1$ off $I$ and $2$ on $I$. The roof area multiplied by $j$ tends uniformly to $\sqrt2$. Dominated convergence, including the continuous rate test, gives the claimed surface law. On all other faces, the contribution for $t\le\epsilon$ is uniformly $O(\int_0^{2\epsilon}(-\log v)\,dv+\epsilon)$ for large $j$, because $dt=dv$ on the coordinate faces and the $s$ endpoint faces have the extra factor $t$. Away from this region there is ordinary trace convergence at rate zero.

For the inverse law, $t/v=1+q_j/v$ separates the ordinary limit $dX/t$ from the excess $q_j\log[(1-q_j)/(e^{-j}D+e^{-2j})]$ at each $s$. The excess is uniformly bounded, concentrates at $t=0$, and tends pointwise to $1+\mathbf1_I$. Dividing by $M_jc_j$ gives the unscaled normalized density, with no extra rate-zero defect by the positive-rate calculation below. To see failure of log-concavity directly, let $a=\min I$. Take equal small intervals centered at $a-3\epsilon$ and $a+\epsilon$ with half-length less than $\epsilon/2$. Their midpoint interval has the same length and lies entirely to the left of $a$. One input has twice the mass of the other, while the midpoint mass equals the smaller one. This violates log-concavity for each density.

For positive rate $r$, change variables $v=c_j^{-1}e^{-jr/\rho}$. At this level $t=q_j+v$. Its allowed $s$ satisfy $e^{-j}D(s)\le c_j^{-1}e^{-jr/\rho}-e^{-2j}$. Away from $r=\rho,2\rho$, the allowed sets tend almost everywhere in $s$ to the three stated regimes. The density in $ds\,dr\,d(x/t)$ is $jt/(M_jc_j\rho)$, which tends locally uniformly for positive $r$ to $2/(c\rho)$. It is bounded uniformly on compact positive-rate intervals, including intervals containing either threshold, so dominated convergence establishes the conditional law and absence of atoms there. Integrating it over the positive rates recovers the entire inverse defect computed by the raw reciprocal primitive. For the displayed anchor, $h(n_0,(s,0,0))=\sqrt2/3$, $L(o)=2c/3$ and $M=1/2$. In the compensated surface tail the two coefficients $\sqrt2$ and $2\sqrt2$ are divided by $\rho$ and $2\rho$ respectively. This proves the stated exact normalization.

For the ordinary row, let $Z_j=\int_{K_j}dX/v$ and $\rho_j=dX/(Z_jv)$ on $K_j$. Its mark $Y_j=\int X\,d\rho_j$ satisfies $L_j(Y_j)=c_jM_j/Z_j$ by affineness and $\int L_j\,d\rho_j=L_j(Y_j)$. Consequently the reweighted row $(L_j/L_j(Y_j))\rho_j$ is normalized original volume and $\rho_j/L_j(Y_j)$ is the normalized reciprocal measure. The ordinary raw reciprocal component has first $x,y$ moments $1/4$ each. For the symmetric $I$, $Z_j\to1+1+|I|=7/3$ and $s$ has mean $1/2$, so the limiting mark is $(1/2,3/28,3/28)$. For all the specified $I$ the mark is strictly interior because the ordinary component has full support in the product and the extra component lies in its closure. The marked value has a positive limit.

For the geometric-cell assertion use the uniformly positive-height anchor case of the positive-rate inverse slice theorem. On that geometric active cell the volume law has its full convex level section and the restricted inverse mass is bounded by the total inverse mass. These are precisely the inputs used by the projection and coarea proof.

For the split rows, use the same identities with $Z_j$ and $M_j$ restricted to the corresponding measurable part. The resulting marks belong to $K_j$ by convexity, and the affine identity holds even for the nonconvex union of the two outer pieces. The raw limit on each part has positive ordinary component and the added boundary measure just computed restricts without boundary atoms in $s$. The limits of the two means are strictly interior, in particular their $s$ means are both $1/2$ by symmetry and the $x,y$ means are positive with $x+y<1$. Each part has positive limiting volume and finite positive limiting raw reciprocal mass. This gives the core, weight and value bounds, as well as the partition of original volume. Restriction of the positive-rate inverse law to the outer pieces, with the appropriate positive row normalization, has exactly their disconnected support. This failure applies to freely split source labels. The single affine geometry used throughout remains convex.

statement:
Let $I$ be any nontrivial closed interval strictly inside $[0,1]$, put $t=x+y$, and take
$$
K_j=\{0\le s\le1,\ x,y\ge0:\ j^{-1}+e^{-j}\operatorname{dist}(s,I)\le t\le1\},\qquad
L_j=c_j(t-j^{-1}+e^{-2j})
$$
with volume-mean logarithm zero. Then $K_j\to[0,1]\times\{x,y\ge0,\ t\le1\}$, $M_j=|K_j|\to1/2$ and $c_j\to c=e^{1/2}$. On the exposed zero edge, with normal $n_0=(0,-1,-1)/\sqrt2$, the boundary negative-log defect and normalized reciprocal-volume defect have tangential densities $\sqrt2(1+\mathbf1_I)$ and $(2/c)(1+\mathbf1_I)$, respectively. They have full support and fail log-concavity. There is a single exact affine contact row with a uniformly interior mark and marked value bounded below, and its original-volume reweighting is uniform on $K_j$.

For $\rho>0$, use rates $r_j=(\rho/j)(-\log L_j)_+$. In physical coordinates $(s,0,0)$ the boundary defect with rate retained is
$$
\sqrt2\,\mathbf1_{[0,1]\setminus I}\,ds\,\delta_\rho
+2\sqrt2\,\mathbf1_I\,ds\,\delta_{2\rho},
$$
and the positive-rate inverse conditionals have density $2/(c\rho)$ on $[0,1]$ for $0<r<\rho$, the same density on $I$ for $\rho<r<2\rho$, and zero for $r>2\rho$. In particular the surface law at the single rate $\rho$ has disconnected tangential support. For $I=[1/3,2/3]$ the one-row mark tends to $(1/2,3/28,3/28)$ and its value to $3c/14$. With anchor $o=(1/2,1/3,1/3)$ the radial reciprocal-rate surface tail and $M L(o)$ times the inverse conditional both have density $2/(3\rho)$ on the indicated intervals.

A geometric active cell of a finite affine minimum with coefficientwise convergence and a uniformly positive-height anchor has the decreasing $1/(d-1)$-concave conditional law of the positive-rate slice theorem if its limiting affine gradient is nonzero and its inverse mass is uniformly bounded. For that same symmetric $I$, split the affine row into $s\in[0,1/4]\cup[3/4,1]$ and its complement, normalize each inverse restriction and take its own mean as its mark. The resulting two exact affine contact rows retain uniform interior source balls and positive limiting weights and values. Their original-volume reweightings, with the row weights, partition original volume. For $0<r<\rho$ the first row has a disconnected positive-rate conditional, although the full geometric affine slice has a convex conditional support.
title: Two exponential rates on one actual affine fiber and disconnected labeled slices
